meta.title: CareLink Menubar: your glucose in the Mac menu bar
hero.title:
Your glucose,
one glance away.
hero.lead: CareLink Menubar puts your MiniMed CareLink readings in the Mac menu bar and on your desktop, so you can stay focused on your work without reaching for your phone.
hero.fineprint: Free and open source · macOS 14 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel
trust.private: Private: your data stays on your Mac
features.title: Everything you check, without the checking
features.lead: The numbers you look at most, always visible, with gentle colour cues when something needs your attention.
f1.title: Always in view
f1.text: Your current glucose and trend arrow live in the menu bar, with a small chart of the last three hours. Orange or red when you're out of range.
f2.title: Time in range at a glance
f2.text: See your last 24 hours in range, below and above, plus your average, variability and GMI, in one clear card.
f3.title: Know when to change
f3.text: Reservoir, pump battery, infusion set and sensor time left. They turn orange and then red as the change gets close.
f4.title: Desktop widgets
f4.text: Three widget sizes for your desktop, with your real recent trend drawn behind the number.
f5.title: Share in one click
f5.text: Copy a clean picture of your current status and paste it into a message to your care team or family.
f6.title: Helpful reminders
f6.text: Optional notifications when your sensor or infusion set is ending, or when new readings stop arriving.
widgets.title: Beautiful on your desktop
widgets.lead: Pick the size that fits your workflow. Click any widget to open the full panel.
privacy.title: Your data stays with you
privacy.lead: Built for people who care about their health data as much as we do.
p1.title: 🔒 Official sign-in
p1.text: You sign in on MiniMed's own CareLink page. The app never sees or stores your password.
p2.title: 🔑 Keychain only
p2.text: Your session is kept in the macOS Keychain on your Mac, not in files.
p3.title: 🚫 No tracking
p3.text: No analytics, no ads and no servers of ours. The app talks only to CareLink.
p4.title: 👁️ Read-only by design
p4.text: It can only read what CareLink already shows you. It cannot change your therapy or your pump.
install.title: Install in three steps
install.lead: It takes about a minute. The extra step on first launch is normal for free apps that are not distributed through Apple.
s1.title: Download and drag
s1.text: Open CareLink-Menubar.dmg and drag the app onto the Applications folder.
s2.title: Open it once
s2.text: Open CareLink Menubar from Applications. macOS says it can't verify the app. Click Done.
s3.title: Allow it
s3.text: Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway. Done: the app appears in your menu bar.
install.note: Why the warning? Apple charges developers a yearly fee to "notarize" apps. CareLink Menubar is free and its code is public, so you can see exactly what it does. You only approve it once for each new version.
faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: Short answers to what people usually ask.
q1: Is this an official MiniMed app?
a1: No. CareLink Menubar is an independent, unofficial app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by MiniMed (formerly Medtronic Diabetes). It reads the same data you can see in CareLink.
q2: Can it change my pump or my insulin?
a2: No. It is read-only by design: it never sends commands to your pump and never changes your therapy.
q3: Does it replace my pump or phone alarms?
a3: No. Keep relying on your pump, sensor and the MiniMed app and their alarms. Always confirm values in the official app before making treatment decisions.
a4: It works with CareLink accounts in both regions: Europe and other countries (which covers every country except the United States, including Canada, Australia and Latin America) and the United States. Accounts can be a patient, or a care partner with one linked patient. It was developed and tested with a MiniMed Flex on a European account; US accounts and other pumps are supported but haven't been verified with real data yet.
a5: A Mac with macOS 14 Sonoma or later (Apple Silicon or Intel) and your CareLink login.
a6: Yes. It's open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0 license, with no subscriptions and no in-app purchases.
a7: Only on your Mac. On first launch you're asked for consent. Readings for the widget are stored locally, and you can withdraw consent at any time to delete them and sign out.
a8: Yes. The app is in English and European Portuguese. By default it follows your Mac's language, and you can switch it any time in Settings → General.
final.title: Ready when you are
